record.original_question: (Hadamard convolutions) Suppose that α ≥ 1, β ≥ 1 and that φ is analytic in D, and satisfies (1 + xz)α φ(z) ∗ 6= 0, |x| = 1, |z| < 1. (1 − z)β Is it true that (1 + xz)α−1 φ(z) ∗ 6= 0, |x| = 1, |z| < 1 ? (1 − z)β This is true when α is a natural number. For the proof and further background, see Sheil-Small [709]. (T. Sheil-Small)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disc. For two functions $f(z)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a_n z^n$ and $g(z)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} b_n z^n$ analytic in $\mathbb{D}$, define their Hadamard convolution (Hadamard product) by
$$ (f * g)(z) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a_n b_n z^n, \qquad z\in\mathbb{D}. $$

Fix real numbers $\alpha\ge 1$ and $\beta\ge 1$. Let $\varphi$ be analytic in $\mathbb{D}$ and assume that
$$ \left( \frac{(1+xz)^{\alpha}}{(1-z)^{\beta}} \right) * \varphi(z) \;\neq\; 0 \qquad \text{for all } |x|=1 \text{ and all } z\in\mathbb{D}. $$

Question: Must it then follow that
$$ \left( \frac{(1+xz)^{\alpha-1}}{(1-z)^{\beta}} \right) * \varphi(z) \;\neq\; 0 \qquad \text{for all } |x|=1 \text{ and all } z\in\mathbb{D}\,? $$

(It is known that the implication holds whenever $\alpha$ is a positive integer. The problem is to decide whether it holds for all real $\alpha\ge 1$.)
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not turn up a definitive resolution of this Hadamard-convolution non-vanishing question for non-integer $\alpha$. The integer-$\alpha$ case is classical (Sheil-Small), but no published full proof or counterexample for general real $\alpha\ge 1$ was located, so the status appears unknown / likely still open.
